description: The name Rosella was chosen as it is a native Australian bird with red and blue coloured feathers which aligns with flame colours.
summary: PyRosella is a web-based dashboard that runs using OpenAI infrastructure to help summarize, compare and visualize differences between collected data with interactive display of flame data. This address the challenge of processing large amounts of data
details:
Pyrosella is currently a local web-based, interactive dashboard with integrated with SI model to visualize and summarize microgravity combustion data from the PSI databased. This project is built using React for frontend, Python as backend pipeline. This project was running on 16GB GPU and Intel i5 CPU on Windows.


The initial launch page presents the top 10 most relevant combustion studies under default environmental settings. The ranking system is achieving using an evaluation matrix factoring time of publication, access frequency, and file data coverage (types of data). Users can choose a study of their interest for the dashboard to model with premade line art of pressurized rovers, satellites, and space stations. A feature that was planned but unfortunately wasn't able to be completed was: If combustion data is available, PyRosella will then attempt to match the parameters of the research to a pre-computed OpenFOAM CFD simulation through a lookup table in the back to instantly display estimated temperature and therefore flammability.

This project aims to make the dense research files more intuitive using visuals to aid development of safety metrics in space development. The logic of this coding set up also reduces the runtime required by using off-line files and look up table that avoids the possibility of crashing due to rendering.


PyRosella is created to make learning and research easier for professors, students, researchers and engineers through visualization and interaction. It is designed to help mission planners to instantly flag high probability and high-risk events based on historical experiments. Therefore, to ensure a safe design of next-generation fire detection systems for crewed/uncrewed mission.
